caption:
New public holidays announced! Nov 7 is now a general holiday, and Durga Puja sees a 5-day break.

The government has declared November 7 a public holiday to mark National Revolution and Solidarity Day. This observance has been included in the Category ‘Ka’ list of national and international days.

The decision was made during the 23rd cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at the Secretariat.

Additionally, the government has declared October 22 a holiday by executive order for Durga Puja, ensuring a continuous five-day holiday for the Hindu community.

To compensate for the additional holiday, all government, autonomous, and semi-autonomous offices will remain open on Saturday, October 17.

According to the Cabinet Division, November 7 will now be a general holiday every year for National Revolution and Solidarity Day.

topic: attack on journalists at rajshahi university
headline_marked: RU attack: [[Case filed against unknown suspects]] despite video evidence
headline: RU attack: Case filed against unknown suspects despite video evidence
summary: Journalists and teachers at Rajshahi University are protesting after a case was filed against 'unknown' persons following an attack that left 10 injured.
details: At least 10 people, including four journalists, were injured when a group of students attacked them with sticks at Rajshahi University (RU) on Sunday night.
The attack occurred near the gate of Shahid Ziaur Rahman Hall after journalists began filming a group of students who had entered the hall to search room 214.
A case was filed on Monday by the hall's deputy registrar, but it names 'unknown' suspects, sparking outrage among campus journalists and teachers.
Critics argue that the suspects are easily identifiable through multiple video recordings of the incident and are known to other students on campus.
Allegations have surfaced that the attack was led by RU Chhatra Dal vice-president Ahsan Habib, though the case does not mention any specific student organization.
Journalists and students held a protest in front of the university administration building, accusing the administration of protecting terrorists.
University Vice-Chancellor Professor Md. Faridul Islam denied giving any favors to any group, stating that 99 students have been punished for various offenses in the last six months.
The Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) has also condemned the attack and urged BNP and Jamaat to strengthen party accountability and end violence.
caption:
10 injured, video evidence available, yet the suspects remain 'unknown' in the official case. What is happening at Rajshahi University?

At least 10 people, including four journalists, were injured when a group of students attacked them with sticks at Rajshahi University (RU) on Sunday night.

The attack occurred near the gate of Shahid Ziaur Rahman Hall after journalists began filming a group of students who had entered the hall to search room 214.

A case was filed on Monday by the hall's deputy registrar, but it names 'unknown' suspects, sparking outrage among campus journalists and teachers.

Critics argue that the suspects are easily identifiable through multiple video recordings of the incident and are known to other students on campus.

Allegations have surfaced that the attack was led by RU Chhatra Dal vice-president Ahsan Habib, though the case does not mention any specific student organization.

Journalists and students held a protest in front of the university administration building, accusing the administration of protecting terrorists.

University Vice-Chancellor Professor Md. Faridul Islam denied giving any favors to any group, stating that 99 students have been punished for various offenses in the last six months.

The Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) has also condemned the attack and urged BNP and Jamaat to strengthen party accountability and end violence.
